description: Practice-defined problem parent/child pairs for the 'Organise problems' canvas's suggestion tray, ADDITIONAL to (never a replacement for) the live SNOMED-descendant search. Each entry is a pair Medicus/SNOMED does not model as a genuine IS-A hierarchy, but that this practice considers a real clinical parent/child relationship worth suggesting. childConceptId/parentConceptId are the only fields actually matched (by conceptId, against the patient's own active problem list) -- description/note are for a human reading this file, never displayed verbatim. Never auto-applied: every suggestion built from an entry here still goes through the same explicit per-link confirm as a SNOMED-derived one.

pairs.note: Pseudophakia (an artificial lens implant) is the expected post-operative state after cataract extraction -- a real clinical sequela, but not a SNOMED IS-A descendant of cataract (different hierarchy branch entirely), so the live descendant search never finds it. Added 2026-08-08 (Nick's first entry on this list).

UNLIKE the pseudophakia entry above, this one IS believed to be a genuine SNOMED IS-A descendant of cataract (Nick confirmed it sits under the cataract hierarchy) -- added here as a pragmatic workaround because problem-nesting.js's own live descendant-search mechanism (the pairHits two-step combined-then-attribute query) was NOT finding it for a real patient. Root cause unconfirmed -- candidates: the combined query's constrainingParentConcepts comma-list (built from every OTHER active problem's own conceptId) may silently truncate/behave unexpectedly at some length; or the specific recorded 'Cataract' problem on that record may carry a different/synonym conceptId than 193570009. Worth a live console probe (constrainingParentConcepts=193570009&query=53889007 directly) if this keeps happening for other genuinely-SNOMED pairs, rather than adding every miss here piecemeal.

CORRECTED 2026-08-20 after Nick reported the first cut (1359971008, FSN 'Extraction of lens by phacoemulsification (procedure)') wasn't matching a real patient's own recorded problem -- 84149000 (FSN 'Aspiration of cataract by phacoemulsification (procedure)') is the code actually used/recorded for this in practice. Confirmed via the public NHS termbrowser API (release v20260729) that 84149000 IS-A both 112963003 'Aspiration of cataract' and 1359971008 (the original entry's own concept) -- a more specific descendant of it, on the same Procedure axis, still NOT a descendant of Cataract (193570009, Disorder/Clinical-finding axis) itself. Same relationship shape as the pseudophakia entry above: a real clinical sequela of a cataract problem (the extraction procedure), different hierarchy branch entirely, so the live descendant search would never surface it on its own. Requested 2026-08-20 alongside a request to always offer this pairing regardless of hierarchy nuance.

Kept alongside 84149000 (2026-08-20 review fix). The first live pick was this broader parent concept; it did not match the patient who motivated the correction, but other records may still carry 1359971008 (or a synonym) rather than the more specific 84149000. Matching is by conceptId only, so both codes need their own pair or one practice's phrasing silently never suggests.
